Each prompt names ONLY the moving part and ends with 'Nothing else moves.' — naming what should stay still backfires, because the model treats those nouns as things to paint (the window-prompt lesson). `example` is the state shown in the artifact and is the pilot subject for that id. cliff_falls no longer exists as a group (all 5 pieces removed 2026-08-29, quota frozen to 0). DECLINED and deliberately absent: A3 sleeping_giants, C8 signposts, G4 ferns, G5 cliff_vines, L5 toadstool_rings, L9 frost_flowers.

_declined_note: `declined` records briefs he has rejected outright. animate_motion reads `animations` only, so anything here is inert — it is kept so a later pass can see these were decided, not overlooked.
_loop_note: From 2026-08-29 every revised prompt closes the loop explicitly — the last frame returns to the first, and nothing may darken below frame one. Added after he reported 'dark paint entering the animation at the end' on R27, where the final frame drained to brown instead of coming back to gold.
_scale_note: 2026-08-29: the three worst results all showed the WHOLE OBJECT rescaling between frames, and in each the moving thing WAS the subject, filling the sprite. Every success so far moves a small fraction of the image instead — a lantern on a post, a bird on a totem. Revised prompts now add 'Nothing in the picture may change size, shape or position' and prefer a subject that occupies little of the frame.
_sundial_note: The sundial shadow (N19, U6, U27) has been offered in three separate lists and passed over every time. Not proposing it again.
_calmer_note: Do not use the word 'calmer' in a prompt. Measured: S1 went 4.5% -> 19.5% when asked to be barely visible, and Q19 5.3% -> 15.8%. State the motion concretely instead — 'each shifting by a single pixel' — and say what does not move.
_copy_note: THE COPY TAIL: 'Everything else in the picture is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel, unchanged in shape, size, position and colour.' State the hold as a COPY, never as a prohibition -- a material noun in a prompt is a thing to PAINT (the window lesson), so 'the stone arch does not move' paints a new arch. A copy instruction names nothing. MEASURED on the 12 batch-X redos (2026-08-29), and it does NOT work everywhere: it fixes the case where the moving thing is a SEPARATE object resting on or hanging off the piece (X24 market awning stopped flashing black, 21.5%->8.9%; X6 shrine 8.1%->4.0%; X20, X23, X25, X65 all steadier). It does NOT fix the case where the moving thing is LIGHT ON THE PIECE'S OWN SURFACE -- X39 ice roses, X46 frozen ice, X34 mushroom gills and X5 beacon post all still repaint their whole body, because there is no seam for the generator to copy across. For that shape, expect to reject rather than re-prompt. X18 (well) got WORSE, 15.3%->22.9%: the snow on the roof is what animates, and no wording has stopped it.
_light_dies_note: NEW FAULT, batch Y (2026-08-29): on a LIT piece the fire or glow can FADE AWAY across the loop instead of flickering -- a torch that ends unlit (Y2), a white blaze that shrinks to a candle (Y11), a pool of lantern light that disappears at frame 3 (Y6), a lantern that dims out (Y20), a gold spiral that loses its shape (Y35). Distinct from the whole-object repaint the copy tail addresses: here the named part is the ONLY thing that changes, and it changes by going out. The drift metric caught all five (29-61%). Candidate wording for the next attempt, untested: ask for the light to return to full brightness in the last frame by name, rather than relying on the generic 'last frame matches the first'.
_flag_accuracy_note: MY OWN FLAGS ARE NOT VERDICTS, AND THE RECORD IS BAD. Batch X: flagged 7, he kept 4 and asked to redo 9 I had passed. Batch Y: flagged 5, he redid none of them. Batch Z: flagged 7, he kept ALL of them and redid one I had passed. Across three batches my flags have predicted his judgement roughly never. Present them as a shortlist to LOOK at, low in the page, never as a recommendation, and never delete on my own read alone.
_rigid_note: THE RIGID-BODY CLAUSE ('It moves as one solid piece and keeps exactly the same shape, size and colours the whole time it moves. It is never redrawn, never reshaped and never changes its outline.') MEASURED 2026-08-29 on Y22/Y24: it does NOT reliably stop a shaped detail inside the moving object being redrawn -- Y22's swing seat still lost its backrest mid-loop. Keep using it (it costs nothing) but do not expect it to save a hung object with fine internal detail.
_light_starts_off_note: A LIT PIECE CAN COME ON LATE as well as go out: Y24's lantern was dark for frames 1-3. FIX CONFIRMED 2026-08-29: adding 'It is lit and clearly visible in every single frame, including the first' put the flame in all five frames. Now on every LIT brief as standard.
_narrowing_note: NARROWING THE NAMED PART IS THE STRONGEST LEVER FOUND SO FAR. Y13 went 21.5%->5.5% motion and 29.5%->3.0% drift purely by changing 'the green surface of the brew bubbles' to 'the small green surface at the very top of the brew moves'. Name the smallest possible region and give it a position ('at the very top', 'at the two ends', 'inside the arch'); the generator holds everything outside a region it can locate.
_ramp_note: THE GLOW RAMP AND ITS FIX. Asking a glow to 'brighten a little and return' is read as a RAMP: the generator starts at full brightness and slides down, so the last frame is darkest and the light can vanish (batch Z: 6 of 15 drained, drift median 25.7%, worst 61.8%). FIX, MEASURED on 20 glows in batch AA (2026-08-29): add 'It is at its brightest in the MIDDLE of the animation and back to exactly its first-frame brightness and colour at the end. It never fades out and is never dimmer at the end than at the start.' Result: drift median 25.7% -> 18.5%, only 2 of 20 ending badly dark. The strips confirm the SHAPE changed -- these peak mid-animation and come back. NEW SIDE EFFECT to solve next: OVER-BRIGHTNESS at the peak. Three blew out to near-white and lost their own colours for a frame (A44 mushrooms, A39 stump, A45). Untested next step: cap the peak -- 'slightly brighter, never white, and it keeps its own colour at every moment'.
_family_scores: MEASURED MEDIANS across X/Y/Z/AA/AB (motion %, drift %). FLAME: finished -- 8.8/7.4/3.5/10.2 motion, blowout ~0, no bad result since the lit-in-every-frame clause. SMOKE: new and working, see _smoke_note. WATER: 3.8/7.5/5.5, settled and nearly exhausted. HANGING: drift 22.6 -> 16.4 once the mover-copy clause became standard; that clause produced the single biggest improvement measured here (A15, 18.6->7.2 motion). GLOW: blowout solved, drift still open at ~21%. FOLIAGE: worst every time it appeared (20.8/22.6/24.8); proposed none since batch Z. AWNINGS: failed twice on the same piece, do not re-propose. FRINGE: works.
_asking_for_more_note: ASKING FOR MORE MOVEMENT MOSTLY DOES NOT WORK. U25 (puffball) improved 1.4%->10.8% when asked for a clearly visible puff, but Z45 (stall awning) went 5.5%->4.3% under the same treatment. A piece that measures near zero is usually one where the named part is small and surrounded by busier detail; the generator ignores it. Prefer to drop rather than re-prompt a third time.
_peak_cap_note: CAPPING THE PEAK ('It only ever gets SLIGHTLY brighter: never white, never washed out, and it keeps its own colour at every single moment.') MEASURED over 20 glows in batch AB: it FIXES BLOWOUT -- median 1.4%, against three pieces washing out entirely in AA -- and does NOT fix drift (21.4% vs 18.5% before). These are two separate faults; the cap solves one. THE ESCAPE PROBLEM, seen twice now: constrain brightness and the generator changes something else instead. A39 grew horns on a stump; B33/B34 MULTIPLIED the glowing fungi, more of them at the end than the start. Always pair a cap with the copy tail, and expect the next fault to appear in whatever degree of freedom is left open.
_mover_copy_note: A COPY INSTRUCTION FOR THE MOVING OBJECT ITSELF ('The thing that moves is only MOVED, never redrawn: its own detail is copied from the first frame exactly -- every line, every edge, every colour, the same number of parts in the same places.'). The standard copy tail protects everything AROUND the named part and says nothing about the part, so the generator redraws the very thing it was told to move. MEASURED 2026-08-29: A15 fish rack 18.6->7.2 motion and 31.6->8.9 drift, the biggest single improvement any prompt change has produced; A24 swing 25.8->16.5. A16 did not take. Now standard on every hanging brief.
_smoke_note: SMOKE IS A WORKING FAMILY, confirmed THREE times on three different shapes (2026-08-29): B50 a coffee pot (4.9% motion / 5.0% drift), C1 a charcoal kiln (1.8/3.1), G10 a laboratory bottle trailing purple vapour (9.9/11.9). REQUIREMENT: the smoke or steam must already be DRAWN in the sprite. Prompt is the plain narrowing form -- 'the thread of smoke above X rises and curls' -- plus the standard copy tail. Chimneys, censers, cooking pots and kilns are all open.
_no_add_note: CLOSING THE QUANTITY ESCAPE. Seen three times now: constrain brightness and the generator changes HOW MANY things there are instead -- A39 grew horns on a stump, B33/B34 multiplied the glowing fungi and grew a new blob, B18 deleted the grass at the base of a rack. The copy tail says everything else is 'copied exactly' but that is evidently read as a style note, not a count. Added 2026-08-29: 'Nothing anywhere is added and nothing anywhere is removed: every object in the picture is present in every frame, the same number of them, in the same places, at the same size.' Judge on the B1/B4/B18/B34/B46 results.
_size_note: PINNING THE SIZE OF A FLAME. B1's lantern flame BALLOONED into a glare lighting the whole well -- flicker was read as grow. Added 2026-08-29: 'It stays exactly the same size and the same shape in every frame -- it never grows, never spreads and never spills past where it already is; only its inner detail shifts.'
_length_note: PIXELLAB CAPS animation_description AT 1000 CHARACTERS. Over it the API answers 422 string_too_long and animate_motion reports a bare FAILED line -- B4 (1009 chars) and B46 (1033) were silently skipped in batch AB before this was found. Clause stacking is what crossed the line, so the clauses are kept COMPACT and PixelLabClient.animate_object now refuses over-long descriptions up front (DESCRIPTION_MAX) instead of letting the API swallow them.
_object_id_note: THE PIXELLAB LINK ON A CANDIDATE PAGE COMES FROM states[STATE].pixellab_object_id, NOT from the piece manifest's top-level 'id' (which is the folder slug) and not from 'object_id' (which does not exist). A selector written as meta.get('object_id') or meta.get('id') silently yields the slug, and every 'Open in PixelLab' link on the page 404s. Introduced around batch Y, found and fixed at batch AC.
_light_vs_object_note: WHEN A GLOW SITS ON MANY SMALL OBJECTS, name the LIGHT, not the objects. 'the glowing fungi brighten' invites the generator to redraw and multiply the fungi (B34 grew new clusters twice, through both the cap and the no-add clause). Try instead: 'the green light ON the fungi brightens a little and returns. The fungi themselves keep exactly the shape, size, position and number they have in the first frame.' Introduced 2026-08-29; judge on B34.
_glow_drift_open: GLOW DRIFT IS THE ONE UNSOLVED FAULT, and four prompt fixes have not moved it: peak-in-the-middle (batch AA), the brightness cap (AB), the no-add clause (AC) and light-vs-object (AC). Measured drift medians for glow: 25.7 (Z) -> 18.5 (AA) -> 21.4 (AB) -> 22.8 (AC), with 5 of 29 still draining away in AC. The other faults in this family ARE solved -- blowout sits at ~1.9% median and multiplication is fixed. RECOMMENDATION: stop writing new clauses for it. Judge glows individually by eye and reject the faders; the marginal prompt is no longer paying.
_single_vs_multi_note: GLOW QUALITY TRACKS EDGE HARDNESS, NOT SHAPE COUNT -- CONFIRMED at batch AH (2026-08-29). AF found the split (crisp 15.8% drift vs soft 34.4%); AH tested it by proposing 28 crisp-edged glows and nothing soft, and drift came in at 12.9% -- THE BEST GLOW RESULT RECORDED IN THIS DOMAIN, against 19.9% when the filter was shape count and 25.7% at its worst. Only 1 of 28 ended badly dark, where it used to be 5 or 6. CRISP = a rune, a seam, a vein, a carved mark, a molten crack, a solid crystal: anything with a hard drawn outline. SOFT = a halo, a ring of light, a bloom across petals, a glow around a stalk. Propose crisp only.

The AE selector took ONE STATE PER PIECE and capped per group, so 173 was a SAMPLE, not the pool. 1,067 sibling states had never been looked at, and 631 of them belong to pieces already animated successfully -- the highest-prior candidates in the domain. _identity_note: THE IDENTITY CLAUSE ('Every object stays the same kind of thing it is in the first frame and keeps its own colour: nothing turns into anything else.') MEASURED on the batch-AD redos 2026-08-29. It WORKS ON CARVED/ENGRAVED SUBJECTS: D47's runes stopped changing letters, drift 3.3->1.8, the best number of the round. It does NOTHING for organic multi-object glows: D33's berries still became white flowers, D45 still bloomed and blew out worse. A carved mark is a shape the generator can hold; a berry is not. Keep the clause -- it is cheap and it fixed the carving -- but do not expect it to rescue a plant.
_stop_redoing_note: STOP REDOING MULTI-OBJECT ORGANIC GLOWS. D33 (berried thicket) and D45 (gold-lit bushes) have now defeated FOUR separate fixes: the brightness cap (AB), the no-add clause (AC), the light-vs-object phrasing (AD) and the identity clause (AD redos). They are the exact class batch AD measured at 27.1% drift against 11.7% for single shapes. Reject rather than write a fifth clause. Redo budget is better spent on single-shape glows, flame and hanging.

He reviews in batches from a phone and reads ids off the page; without the bar he transcribes them by hand ("I really like the feature where I can select things"). The two redo pages shipped without it. Fixed structurally: candidate_page.render_results() builds a results page and always appends _TAIL, which is the bar -- do not hand-assemble a results page.
_numbers_are_not_taste_note: MY METRICS DO NOT PREDICT HIS EYE. The batch-AD redos: I scored D47 the best result of the round (drift 3.3->1.8, identity clause working exactly as designed) and D24 clearly improved; he looked at them and called both ugly, along with six others. Eight of nine removed. Motion %, drift and blowout catch specific FAULTS -- a light dying, a thing blooming, an object multiplying -- and are worth keeping for that. They say nothing about whether an animation is nice to look at. Never present a number as a verdict; show the animation and let him judge.
